extracted.intended_audience: Florida administrative agencies, administrative law judges, regulated parties, attorneys, and petitioners involved in Chapter 120 proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements from Florida's Administrative Procedure Act (Chapter 120) governing use of unadopted rules, records, hearings, protests, mediation, summary hearings, attorney's fees, licensing, investigations, and exemptions. Focused on what agencies, judges, and parties must do and what rights/criteria apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on unadopted rules — general conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may base its action upon unadopted rules when the statute being implemented directs it to adopt rules, the agency has not had time to adopt those rules because the requirement was so recently enacted, and the agency has initiated rulemaking and is proceeding expeditiously and in good faith to adopt the required rules, and the administrative law judge determines that rulemaking is neither feasible nor practicable and the unadopted rules would not constitute an invalid exercise of delegated legislative authority if adopted as rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An unadopted rule shall not be presumed valid; agency bears the burden of demonstration of the prerequisites above.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unadopted rule substantive validity factors (a–f)
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency must demonstrate that the unadopted rule: (a) is within the powers, functions, and duties delegated by the Legislature or constitutional authority; (b) does not enlarge, modify, or contravene the specific provisions of law implemented; (c) is not vague, establishes adequate standards for agency decisions, or does not vest unbridled discretion in the agency; (d) is not arbitrary or capricious (arbitrary = not supported by logic or facts; capricious = adopted without thought or reason or irrational); (e) is not being applied to the substantially affected party without due notice; and (f) does not impose excessive regulatory costs on the regulated person, county, or city.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the specific elements the agency must prove for an unadopted rule to be relied upon; failure on any element undermines reliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency rejection of ALJ determination on unadopted rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The administrative law judge’s determination regarding an unadopted rule shall not be rejected by the agency unless the agency first determines from a review of the complete record, and states with particularity in the order, that such determination is clearly erroneous or does not comply with essential requirements of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a court finds the agency’s rejection does not comport with this standard, agency action is set aside and the court shall award prevailing party reasonable costs and attorney fees for the initial proceeding and the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collateral challenge and consolidation
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner may pursue a separate, collateral challenge under s. 120.56 even if an adequate remedy exists through a proceeding under this section; the administrative law judge may consolidate the proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits multiple procedural avenues and consolidation for efficiency; parties should be aware dual tracks may be pursued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record composition for de novo proceedings (subsection f)
rubrics_metrics.description: The record shall consist only of: 1. All notices, pleadings, motions, and intermediate rulings; 2. Evidence admitted; 3. Those matters officially recognized; 4. Proffers of proof and objections and rulings thereon; 5. Proposed findings and exceptions; 6. Any decision, opinion, order, or report by the presiding officer; 7. All staff memoranda or data submitted to the presiding officer during the hearing or prior to its disposition, after notice of the submission to all parties, except advisory staff communications permitted under s. 120.66(1) if public records; 8. All matters placed on the record after an ex parte communication; 9. The official transcript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits the record to enumerated items; excludes other materials not explicitly listed; staff advisory communications excluded unless public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation and access to testimony/transcripts
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall accurately and completely preserve all testimony in the proceeding, and, on the request of any party, it shall make a full or partial transcript available at no more than actual cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties can obtain transcripts at cost; agencies must ensure complete preservation for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary final order standard (no genuine issue of material fact)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party may move for a summary final order when there is no genuine issue as to any material fact. A summary final order shall be rendered if the administrative law judge determines from pleadings, depositions, answers to interrogatories, admissions on file, together with affidavits if any, that no genuine issue as to any material fact exists and that the moving party is entitled as a matter of law to entry of a final order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summary final order mirrors civil summary judgment principles; the order must include findings of fact, conclusions of law, disposition/penalty if applicable, and other legally required information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relinquishment of jurisdiction to agency
rubrics_metrics.description: When a dispute of material fact no longer exists, any party may move the administrative law judge to relinquish jurisdiction to the agency. An order relinquishing jurisdiction shall be rendered if the judge determines from pleadings, depositions, answers, admissions, and affidavits that no genuine issue exists. If relinquished, the agency may promptly conduct a proceeding under subsection (2), but parties may not raise factual issues that could have been raised before the judge. An order relinquishing jurisdiction need not contain findings of fact, conclusions of law, or a recommended disposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relinquishment stops ALJ adjudication and returns matter to agency subject to limits on raising new factual issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Findings of fact standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Findings of fact shall be based upon a preponderance of the evidence, except in penal or licensure disciplinary proceedings or as otherwise provided by statute, and shall be based exclusively on the evidence of record and on matters officially recognized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies burden/standard of proof for fact-finding in administrative hearings; exceptions for disciplinary matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended order contents and exception period
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer shall submit a recommended order consisting of findings of fact, conclusions of law, recommended disposition or penalty if applicable, and any other information required by law. The agency shall allow each party 15 days to submit written exceptions to the recommended order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended orders are de novo; parties have a fixed period (15 days) to raise exceptions before agency action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final order must rule on exceptions and exception specificity requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The final order shall include an explicit ruling on each exception, but an agency need not rule on an exception that does not clearly identify the disputed portion of the recommended order by page number or paragraph, does not identify the legal basis for the exception, or does not include appropriate and specific citations to the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions must be specific in location, legal basis, and record citations or agency may ignore them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency modification/rejection of recommended order — standards and required particularity
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency may reject or modify the conclusions of law or interpretations of administrative rules over which it has substantive jurisdiction, but when rejecting/modifying such conclusions it must state with particularity its reasons and must find that its substituted conclusion or interpretation is as or more reasonable than that rejected. Rejection/modification of conclusions of law may not form the basis for rejection/modification of findings of fact. The agency may not reject or modify findings of fact unless it first determines from review of the entire record and states with particularity that the findings were not based upon competent substantial evidence or that proceedings did not comply with essential requirements of law. The agency may accept the recommended penalty but may not reduce or increase it without review of the complete record and stating with particularity its reasons, citing the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires particularized, record-supported explanations for deviations from ALJ recommended findings/conclusions; protects factual findings unless clearly unsupported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely filing of final order and notice to division
rubrics_metrics.description: If a recommended order is submitted to an agency, the agency shall provide a copy of its final order and any exceptions to the division within 15 days after the order is filed with the agency clerk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures division receives agency final orders and exceptions promptly (15 days).

rubrics_metrics.name: Director authority to reconcile conflicting time requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When statutes or rules impose conflicting time requirements for scheduling expedited hearings or issuance of recommended or final orders, the director of the division shall have authority to set the proceedings for orderly operation of the chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides central scheduling authority to resolve statutory or rules conflicts on timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and opportunity in proceedings without disputed material facts
rubrics_metrics.description: In hearings with no disputed issues of material fact the agency shall: 1) Give reasonable notice to affected persons of the action and a summary of factual, legal, and policy grounds; 2) Give parties or counsel the option to present written or oral evidence in opposition or a written statement challenging the grounds; 3) If objections are overruled, provide a written explanation within 7 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures basic notice, participation opportunity, and prompt written explanations in non-disputed proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on basing agency action on unadopted or invalid rule in non-disputed hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may not base agency action that determines the substantial interests of a party on an unadopted rule or a rule that is an invalid exercise of delegated legislative authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict prohibition in non-disputed hearings against reliance on unadopted/invalid rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record composition for non-disputed hearings (subsection 2(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The record shall consist only of: 1) The notice and summary of grounds; 2) Evidence received; 3) All written statements submitted; 4) Any decision overruling objections; 5) All matters placed on the record after an ex parte communication; 6) The official transcript; 7) Any decision, opinion, order, or report by the presiding officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines a narrower record for non-disputed hearings than de novo proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract solicitation protest notice requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall provide notice of a decision or intended decision concerning a solicitation, contract award, or exceptional purchase by electronic posting. This notice must state: 'Failure to file a protest within the time prescribed in section 120.57(3), Florida Statutes, or failure to post the bond or other security required by law within the time allowed for filing a bond shall constitute a waiver of proceedings under chapter 120, Florida Statutes.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic posting is mandatory and must include a warning about waiver for failure to timely protest or post bond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits for filing protests to solicitations or awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person adversely affected shall file a notice of protest in writing within 72 hours after posting of the notice of decision or intended decision. For protests of solicitation terms/conditions/specifications the notice of protest shall be filed within 72 hours after posting of the solicitation. The formal written protest shall be filed within 10 days after the date the notice of protest is filed. Saturdays, Sundays, and state holidays are excluded in computing the 72-hour periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict, short filing deadlines; formal protest must state particularity the facts and law upon which protest is based; failure to timely file constitutes waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency stay of solicitation upon timely formal protest and exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of a timely filed formal written protest, the agency shall stop the solicitation or contract award process until the protest is resolved by final agency action, unless the agency head sets forth in writing particular facts and circumstances requiring continuance without delay to avoid immediate and serious danger to public health, safety, or welfare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserves procurement process status quo pending protest unless documented emergency justification to proceed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to resolve procurement protests by mutual agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall provide an opportunity to resolve the protest by mutual agreement within 7 days (excluding weekends and state holidays) after receipt of a formal written protest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short mandated mediation/settlement window before formal proceedings proceed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral and handling when procurement protest unresolved and facts disputed
rubrics_metrics.description: If not resolved by mutual agreement and if there is a disputed issue of material fact, the agency shall refer the protest to the division by electronic means for proceedings under subsection (1). If no disputed issue of material fact, an informal proceeding under subsection (2) may be conducted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes handling based on whether factual disputes exist; referral triggers expedited ALJ assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited procurement protest hearing timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of a formal written protest referred to the division, the director shall expedite the hearing and assign an ALJ who shall commence a hearing within 30 days after receipt by the division and enter a recommended order within 30 days after the hearing or within 30 days after receipt of the hearing transcript, whichever is later. Each party has 10 days to submit written exceptions to the recommended order. A final order shall be entered by the agency within 30 days of the entry of a recommended order. These time provisions may be waived by stipulation of all parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Very compressed timeframes for procurement protests; parties should be prepared for rapid process or stipulate otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence/submissions limitations in procurement protests
rubrics_metrics.description: In a protest to an invitation to bid or request for proposals, no submissions made after the bid or proposal opening which amend or supplement the bid or proposal shall be considered. In a protest to an invitation to negotiate, no submissions made after the agency announces its intent to award, reject all replies, or withdraw the solicitation which amend or supplement the reply shall be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discourages post-deadline amendments to bids/proposals in protests; enforces finality of submissions at opening/announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden and standards of proof in procurement protests
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise provided by statute, the burden of proof rests with the protesting party. In a competitive-procurement protest (other than rejection of all bids/proposals/replies), the ALJ shall conduct a de novo proceeding to determine whether the agency’s proposed action is contrary to governing statutes, agency rules/policies, or solicitation specifications. The standard of proof is whether the proposed agency action was clearly erroneous, contrary to competition, arbitrary, or capricious. In bid-protest proceedings contesting intended rejection of all bids/proposals/replies, the standard of review is whether the agency’s intended action is illegal, arbitrary, dishonest, or fraudulent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different standards depending on protest type; protesting party bears burden to demonstrate agency action meets the listed defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal disposition permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless precluded by law, informal disposition may be made of any proceeding by stipulation, agreed settlement, or consent order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties and agencies can settle by agreement absent statutory prohibition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-applicability to preliminary investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: This section does not apply to agency investigations preliminary to agency action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural protections described are inapplicable to preliminary investigative activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mediation availability and tolling
rubrics_metrics.description: Each announcement of an agency action that affects substantial interests shall advise whether mediation is available and that choosing mediation does not affect the right to an administrative hearing. If the agency and all parties agree to mediation in writing within 10 days after the announcement’s election period, time limitations under ss. 120.569 and 120.57 shall be tolled to allow mediation. Mediation shall be concluded within 60 days unless otherwise agreed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agreement to mediate tolls statutory filing deadlines; mediation timeline default is 60 days; parties must agree in writing within the stated window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mediation agreement content and outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: The mediation agreement shall include mediator selection, allocation of costs and fees associated with mediation, and the mediating parties’ understanding regarding confidentiality of discussions and documents. If mediation results in settlement, the agency shall enter a final order incorporating the agreement. If mediation terminates without settlement, the agency shall notify parties that administrative hearing processes are resumed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agreements must address mediator, costs, confidentiality; settlement becomes final agency order when incorporated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary hearing initial order and timing (Section 120.574(1)(a–c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 5 business days following division’s receipt of a petition or request for hearing, the division shall issue and serve an initial order assigning the case to an ALJ and providing general information about practice and procedure before the division. The initial order shall advise that a summary hearing is available upon agreement of all parties and describe expedited sequences, limited discovery, and final order provisions. Within 15 days after service any party may file a motion for summary hearing; if all original parties agree in writing, the proceeding shall be conducted within 30 days of the agreement. Intervenors are governed by the decision of original parties and have no standing to challenge that decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets procedural windows: 5 business days to initial order, 15 days to move for summary hearing, 30 days target to conduct summary hearing if agreed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted motions in summary hearing process
rubrics_metrics.description: Motions are limited to: 1) opposition to the petition; 2) requesting discovery beyond informal exchange of documents and witness lists (additional discovery only upon showing of necessity and only if it can be completed not later than 5 days prior to final hearing); 3) motion for continuance; 4) motion requesting prehearing conference (or judge may require one) for identifying legal and factual issues, witness names/addresses, documentary evidence, range of penalties, and other matters to expedite resolution; 5) suggestion during/after preliminary hearing that case is no longer appropriate for summary disposition, with possible referral back to formal adjudicatory process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discovery is tightly circumscribed; prehearing conferences focus the issues and witnesses; judge may return case to full adjudication if summary process is inappropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exchange deadlines for documentary evidence in summary hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Not later than 5 days prior to the final hearing, the parties shall furnish to each other copies of documentary evidence and lists of witnesses who may testify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short exchange deadline requires parties to be prepared early; late documentary evidence may be excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights of parties in summary hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: All parties shall have opportunity to respond, present evidence and argument on all issues, conduct cross-examination, submit rebuttal evidence, and be represented by counsel or other qualified representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even in expedited summary hearings, fundamental adversarial rights are preserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record composition for summary hearings (Section 120.574(2)(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The record shall consist only of: 1) All notices, pleadings, motions, and intermediate rulings; 2) Evidence received; 3) A statement of matters officially recognized; 4) Proffers of proof and objections and rulings thereon; 5) Matters placed on the record after an ex parte communication; 6) The written decision of the ALJ presiding at the final hearing; 7) The official transcript of the final hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines what materials comprise the record in summary proceedings; similar but distinct list from de novo records.

rubrics_metrics.name: ALJ decision timing and required contents in summary hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: The ALJ’s decision shall be rendered within 30 days after conclusion of the final hearing or filing of the transcript, whichever is later. The decision, final agency action subject to judicial review, shall include: 1) Findings of fact based exclusively on evidence of record and matters officially recognized; 2) Conclusions of law; 3) Imposition of a fine or penalty, if applicable; 4) Any other information required by law or rule to be in a final order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 30-day deadline and required contents standardize summary hearing outcomes; decision is final agency action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attorney’s fees — award when party acted for improper purpose (120.595(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: In proceedings under s. 120.57(1), the final order shall award reasonable costs and a reasonable attorney’s fee to the prevailing party only where the nonprevailing adverse party has been determined by the ALJ to have participated in the proceeding for an improper purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees are not routinely awarded to prevailing parties; requires a finding of improper purpose by the nonprevailing party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper purpose definition and factors creating rebuttable presumption
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Improper purpose’ means participation primarily to harass, cause unnecessary delay, for frivolous purpose, or to needlessly increase litigation costs. The ALJ shall consider whether the nonprevailing adverse party participated in two or more other such proceedings involving the same prevailing party and same project in which the nonprevailing adverse party did not establish merits; in such event it shall be rebuttably presumed the party participated for an improper purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patterns of repetitive, meritless litigation support fee-shifting; presumption is rebuttable but creates a strong inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: ALJ designation and determination of fee awards
rubrics_metrics.description: In any proceeding where the ALJ determines a party participated for an improper purpose, the recommended order shall so designate and shall determine the award of costs and attorney’s fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee determinations flow from ALJ recommended orders and must be reflected therein.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions for fees: costs, nonprevailing adverse party
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Costs’ has the same meaning as costs allowed in civil actions under chapter 57. ‘Nonprevailing adverse party’ means a party that has failed to have substantially changed the outcome of the proposed or final agency action; if proceeding results in any substantial modification intended to resolve matters raised, the party is not a nonprevailing adverse party. The recommended order shall state whether the change is substantial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies who counts as nonprevailing and what costs include; substantial modifications can prevent fee awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees in challenges to proposed rules (120.595(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a court or ALJ declares a proposed rule or portion invalid under s. 120.56(2), judgment shall be rendered against the agency for reasonable costs and attorney’s fees unless the agency demonstrates its actions were substantially justified or special circumstances make the award unjust. ‘Substantially justified’ means there was a reasonable basis in law and fact at the time actions were taken. If agency prevails, court/ALJ may award fees against a party if it participated for improper purpose. No award shall exceed $50,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages agencies to have reasonable legal/factual basis for proposed rules; sets a $50k cap for these awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees in challenges to existing rules (120.595(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a court or ALJ declares an existing rule or portion invalid under s. 120.56(3) or (5), judgment shall be rendered against the agency for reasonable costs and fees unless agency shows substantial justification or special circumstances. Agency’s actions are ‘substantially justified’ if reasonable basis in law and fact existed at the time. If agency prevails, fees may be awarded against a party for improper purpose. No award shall exceed $50,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parallel standard and $50k cap apply for challenges to existing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and stays for statements alleged to be unadopted rules (120.595(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: If ALJ determines a statement violates s. 120.54(1)(a) or agency must discontinue reliance, judgment for reasonable costs and fees shall be entered unless the statement was required by federal government to implement/retain delegated/approved program or meet condition for federal funds. If the agency publishes a notice of rulemaking under s. 120.54(3)(a) before final hearing, such notice automatically operates as a stay of proceedings pending rulemaking (ALJ may vacate stay for good cause). The ALJ shall award reasonable costs and fees accrued by petitioner prior to the notice date unless the agency proves it did not know and should not have known the statement was an unadopted rule. Attorneys’ fees and costs under this paragraph shall be awarded only upon a finding the agency received notice that the statement may constitute an unadopted rule at least 30 days before a petition under s. 120.56(4) was filed and agency failed to publish required notice addressing the statement within that 30-day period. Notice to agency may be satisfied by receipt of a copy of the petition or similar paper. An award of attorney’s fees under this paragraph may not exceed $50,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides both fee-shifting protections for petitioners and safe-harbor for agencies that promptly publish rulemaking notices; $50k cap applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment source and limitations for attorney fee awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding chapter 284, an award shall be paid from the budget entity of the secretary, executive director, or equivalent administrative officer of the agency, and the agency shall not be entitled to payment of an award or reimbursement for payment of an award under any provision of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies fiscal responsibility for fee awards lies with agency's budget entity and precludes agency reimbursement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency prevailing — fee awards against parties for improper purpose or unsupported claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If the agency prevails, the court/ALJ shall award reasonable costs and attorney’s fees against a party if it determines the party participated for an improper purpose or that the party or the party’s attorney knew or should have known a claim was not supported by the material facts necessary or would not be supported by then-existing law applied to those facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discourages frivolous or knowingly unsupported claims by permitting fee awards against parties/attorneys.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals — court discretion to award fees and when mandatory award arises
rubrics_metrics.description: When there is an appeal, the court in its discretion may award reasonable attorney’s fees and costs to the prevailing party if the court finds the appeal was frivolous, meritless, or an abuse of appellate process, or that the agency action precipitating the appeal was a gross abuse of agency discretion. If the court finds the agency improperly rejected or modified findings of fact in a recommended order, the court shall award reasonable attorney’s fees and costs to a prevailing appellant for the administrative proceeding and the appellate proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows fee awards on appeal in discretionary or mandatory circumstances when agency misconduct or frivolous appeals occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency duty to examine license applications (30-day notice of errors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of a license application, an agency shall examine the application and, within 30 days after such receipt, notify the applicant of any apparent errors or omissions and request any additional information the agency is permitted by law to require. An agency may not deny a license for failure to correct an error or omission or to supply additional information unless the agency timely notified the applicant within this 30-day period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects applicants from late discovery of defects; agency must timely notify of deficiencies within 30 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for applicant to submit additional information and completeness rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency may establish by rule the time period for submitting any additional information requested. For good cause shown, the agency shall grant a request for an extension. If the applicant believes the agency’s request for additional information is not authorized by law or rule, at the applicant’s request the agency shall proceed to process the application. An application is complete upon receipt of all requested information and correction of any error or omission for which the applicant was timely notified or when the time for such notification has expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may compel processing if agency’s requests are unauthorized; completeness defined by requested items or expiration of notice window.

rubrics_metrics.name: License decision deadline and licensure by default
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for a license must be approved or denied within 90 days after receipt of a completed application unless a shorter period is provided by law. The 90-day period is tolled by initiation of a proceeding under ss. 120.569 and 120.57. Any application not approved or denied within the 90-day or shorter period, within 15 days after conclusion of a public hearing on the application, or within 45 days after a recommended order is submitted to the agency and parties, whichever is latest and applicable, is considered approved unless the recommended order recommends denial. Subject to satisfactory completion of any required examination, a license considered approved shall be issued and may include reasonable conditions authorized by law. Any applicant seeking to claim licensure by default must notify the agency clerk in writing of intent to rely upon the default license provision and may not act on the default until receipt of such notice by the agency clerk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes default approval if agency fails to act within specified combined timeframes; applicant must provide written notice to rely on default approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency duty when activity exempt from licensure
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant seeks a license for an activity that is exempt from licensure, the agency shall notify the applicant and return any tendered application fee within 30 days after receipt of the original application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects applicants from paying for unnecessary licensing where exemptions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of decision to grant or deny license
rubrics_metrics.description: Each applicant shall be given written notice, personally or by mail, that the agency intends to grant or deny, or has granted or denied, the application for license. The notice must state with particularity the grounds or basis for issuance or denial, except when issuance is ministerial. Unless waived, copy shall be delivered or mailed to each party’s attorney of record and to each person who requested notice. Each notice must inform recipient of the basis for agency decision, any administrative hearing or judicial review available, indicate procedure that must be followed, and state applicable time limits. The issuing agency shall certify the date notice was mailed or delivered and file notice and certification with the agency clerk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed notice content and filing/serving requirements ensure due process and ability to seek review.

rubrics_metrics.name: License renewal protection
rubrics_metrics.description: When a licensee has made timely and sufficient application for renewal of a license which does not automatically expire by statute, the existing license shall not expire until the application for renewal has been finally acted upon by the agency or, if application is denied or terms limited, until the last day for seeking review of the agency order or a later date fixed by court order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents lapse of licensure during renewal processing and appeal windows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required notice and opportunity before revocation/suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: No revocation, suspension, annulment, or withdrawal of any license is lawful unless prior to the entry of a final order, the agency has served by personal service or certified mail an administrative complaint affording reasonable notice to the licensee of facts or conduct which warrant the intended action and unless the licensee has been given an adequate opportunity to request a proceeding pursuant to ss. 120.569 and 120.57. If personal service cannot be made and certified mail is returned undelivered, the agency shall publish a short, plain notice once each week for 4 consecutive weeks in a newspaper published in the county of the licensee’s last known address; if no newspaper, publish in a newspaper of general circulation in that county.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies methods to provide notice when direct service fails; ensures opportunity to be heard before deprivation of license.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency suspension procedural protections
rubrics_metrics.description: If agency finds immediate serious danger to public health, safety, or welfare requires emergency suspension/restriction/limitation of a license, the agency may take such action by any procedure that is fair under the circumstances provided: (a) procedure provides at least same procedural protection as other statutes/Constitutions; (b) agency takes only that action necessary to protect the public interest; (c) agency states in writing at time of or prior to action the specific facts and reasons for finding immediate danger and reasons for concluding procedure used is fair. The agency’s findings of immediate danger, necessity, and procedural fairness are judicially reviewable. Summary suspension must be followed by prompt suspension/revocation proceeding pursuant to ss. 120.569 and 120.57.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows emergency action but requires written factual justification, proportionality, and later follow-up proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of other agency statements/policies as licensing conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: No agency shall include as a condition of approval of any license any provision that is based upon a statement, policy, or guideline of another agency unless that statement/policy/guideline is within the jurisdiction of the other agency and the other agency identifies the specific legal authority for each such statement/policy/guideline. The licensing agency must provide the licensee an opportunity to challenge the condition as invalid. If the licensing agency bases a condition on another agency’s statement/policy/guideline, any party may require the other agency to join as a party to determine the validity of the condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents agencies from imposing non-jurisdictional policy conditions without legal authority and provides joining mechanism to challenge validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to transcript/recording and counsel in agency investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Every person who responds to a request or demand by any agency for written data or an oral statement shall be entitled to a transcript or recording of his or her oral statement at no more than cost. Any person compelled to appear, or who appears voluntarily, before any presiding officer or agency in an investigation or proceeding has the right, at his or her own expense, to be accompanied, represented, and advised by counsel or other qualified representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects procedural rights of witnesses/respondents in investigations: access to transcript at cost and right to counsel at own expense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administration Commission exemption authority and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administration Commission may exempt any process or proceeding governed by this act from one or more requirements when: (a) agency head certifies that the requirement would conflict with federal law/rules with which agency must comply; (b) to permit persons to receive tax benefits or federal funds under federal law; or (c) when conformity with the requirements would be so inconvenient or impractical as to defeat the purpose of the agency proceeding or the purpose of the act and would not be in the public interest considering nature of intended action and enabling act. Prior to granting an exemption, the commission shall establish alternative procedures to achieve the agency’s purpose consistent, insofar as possible, with intent and purpose of the act. Prior to granting an exemption the commission shall hold a public hearing after notice as provided in s. 120.525.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exemptions are available but require findings, alternative procedures consistent with the act, and a public hearing with notice.
